issue.title: Bug: config load_minigraph will result in missing gbsyncd fields

failure.body: ### Is it platform specific generic (issue was found on Cisco 8800 chassis but it could be generic) ### Importance or Severity High ### Description of the bug Running `sudo config load_minigraph --override_config -y` on Cisco 8800 chassis' upstream LC intermittently (~50% on 202405 image) results in `FEATURE|gbsyncd` entries in per-ASIC `config_db.json` files having only `has_global_scope` and `has_per_asic_scope`, while missing `auto_restart, state, delayed, high_mem_alert, set_owner, support_syslog_rate_limit`. This issue happens more frequently with 202511 image. ### Steps to Reproduce Run `sudo config load_minigraph --override_config -y` on Cisco 8800 chassis' upstream LC ### Actual Behavior and Expected Behavior Actual: `FEATURE|gbsyncd` entries in per-ASIC `config_db.json` files having only `has_global_scope` and `has_per_asic_scope`, while missing `auto_restart, state, delayed, high_mem_alert, set_owner, support_syslog_rate_limit`. Expected: `FEATURE|gbsyncd` entries in per-ASIC `config_db.json` files having all required fields. ### Relevant log output ```shell ``` ### Output of `show version`, `show techsupport` ```shell ``` ### Attach files (if any) _No response_

resolution.title: gbsyncd: use RESTORE REPLACE when cloning FEATURE entries
resolution.description:
Signed-off-by: Anand Mehra (anamehra) <EMAIL>

#### Why I did it
Fixes: #26670

gbsyncd seeds FEATURE and SYSLOG_CONFIG_FEATURE rows for gbsyncd by cloning
the syncd entries through Redis DUMP/RESTORE.
RESTORE without REPLACE fails when destination key exists. In current runtime, featured and gbsyncd can touch the same feature keys during bootstrap, causing intermittent BUSYKEY failures and incomplete seeding.

##### Work item tracking
- Microsoft ADO **(number only)**:

#### How I did it
Use RESTORE with REPLACE so initialization succeeds even when destination keys
already exist (for example when featured updates the same keys first). This
removes bootstrap failures caused by BUSYKEY races while preserving current
design intent: gbsyncd starts with syncd-equivalent config.

#### How to verify it
Bringup sonic-mgmt T2 configuration with deploy-mg.
